applies_why: The judge text disposes of D5 vs C5 by saying [CR2] G leaves the sign's sense open, so it is making a verse-level underdetermination judgment rather than a chain-by-chain footing comparison.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'never verse by verse': I weighed (1) it bars resolving a link by a single verse's open sense instead of weighing the competing chains by footing, against (2) it merely bars a mechanical verse-by-verse tally while allowing an isolated-verse ambiguity finding.
why: The judge leaves the Isaiah 7:14 link underdetermined because the sign's sense is open, which is a verse-level ambiguity judgment rather than the required chain-against-chain weighing by footing.
